newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh lent tacit support to Pol Gen Salang Bunnag in the extra-judical killing of six drug suspects by police. He said the actions of the police team supervised directly by the deputy director-general of the Police Department in Suphan Buri on November 27 had been proper and designed to "get rid of" drug dealers. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said yesterday that he planned to visit Burma at the end of next month or early March, and reiterated that Thailand would stick to its policy of "constructive engagement" with Burma's military junta despite recent unrest in Rangoon. (THE NATION)

- Businessmen want each province to have a deputy governor charged with promoting the local economy. If the chambers of commerce proposal is adopted, it will be the first time top officials directly handling economic issues will be part of Thai provincial administrations. Representatives of 76 chambers would discuss the idea in Trang at their annual meeting this weekend, chamber of commerce secretary Jirayuth Vasurat said yesterday (BUSINESS POST)

- Charoen Pokphand Feedmill Plc, the cornerstone of Thailand's large agro-industrial conglomerates, yesterday announced its first US joint venture in checken farming and processing. With a registered capital of US$34.8 million the new company, Charoen Pokphan (US), will begin operation in early 1998, turning out 52 million chickens a year to be sold mostly in the United States. (THE NATION)
